name: Prawn Stir Fry
author: Nagi

items: 1 1/2 tbsp light soy sauce (sub all purpose soy, Note 1)
1 tbsp Chinese cooking wine (sub Mirin or dry sherry, Note 2)
2 tbsp oil, peanut, canola or vegetable
250g / 8 oz medium prawns, raw, peeled and deveined (equiv. 500g/1lb whole prawns, Note 5)
1 1/2 bunches broccolini, trimmed, cut into 5cm / 2" lengths, (~1 1/2 cups. Sub normal broccoli)
120g / 4 oz snow peas, thin string removed from both sides

method: Steam broccolini: Steam broccolini until crisp-tender, about 2 - 3 minutes (remember it will cook more in the stir fry). Set aside to drain and dry.
Stir Fry Sauce: Put all Stir Fry Sauce ingredients except water into a bowl. Mix until cornflour is dissolved. Then stir in water.

Cook then remove prawns: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet on medium to medium-high heat. Add prawns and spread them in a single layer. Cook for 1 1/2 minutes, then turn and cook the other side for 1 minute until cooked through. Try not to make the prawns too golden (they are only lightly browned in stir fries). Remove prawns to a bowl. Set aside.

Cook onion, garlic and ginger: Add more oil if the pan seems a bit dry. Still on medium-high heat, add onion and cook for 1 minute. Then add ginger and garlic and cook for another 1 minute until onion is starting to soften but not colour.
Add snow peas, then broccolini: Add snow peas and toss until coated with oil. Then add broccolini and toss through.

Add Sauce and thicken: Give the Sauce a stir (to dissolve cornflour settled at bottom), then pour into skillet. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens to syrup consistency (about 1 minute) and coats the ingredients nicely.
Add prawns back in: Then add the prawns back in (including any juices in the bowl). Toss for another 30 seconds until prawns are warmed through.
Serve: Serve with rice!

name: Hailey Bieber Chicken Meatballs
author: Julz Yap
method: Combine all MEATBALL ingredients into a bowl. Roll into 16 small balls.
Heat 1/2 tbsp olive oil in a pan and sear/cook the meatballs. Add another 1/2 tbsp olive oil before turning them over. Set aside.
Pour 1 tbsp olive oil into the same pan, add diced brown onion, and cook until soft and caramelised. Just before it's fully done, stir in minced garlic and cook until aromatic.
Pour in the passata, add 2 tsp sugar and salt, and let it simmer for about 5 minutes.
Return the meatballs to the pan and heat through before serving.
Top with cottage cheese (~40g), parmesan (~10g), and fresh basil.

name: Fish en Papillote (Fish in a Bag)
author: Chef JB (RecipeTin)

items: 160g / 5.6oz x 2 snapper fillets, skin off, pin boned (or other fish fillets, see Note 1)
3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, separated
200g / 7oz kipfler potatoes (fingerling potatoes), peeled and sliced 0.5cm / 0.2" thick – 2 medium (or baby potatoes)
1 red capsicum (bell pepper), cut in half, cored then sliced 0.5cm / 0.2" thick
1/2 red onion, cut into wedges 0.3cm / 0.1″ thick
3/4 tsp cooking salt / kosher salt, separated (half for table salt, 50% extra for flakes)
2 tbsp chardonnay or other dry white wine, (sub low-sodium vegetable stock/broth) (Note 3)

method: Preheat oven to 190°C / 375°F (170°C fan-forced).

Cook potato - Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes and cook for 4 minutes, stirring regularly (use 2 wooden spoons if needed). They should pick up a little colour but not too much.
Cook the rest of vegetables - Add the zucchini, capsicum, red onion, garlic and half of the salt and pepper. Toss everything together for about 1 minute, then set aside.

Place two pieces of foil on your work surface (50cm / 20" long x 30cm / 12" wide), then top with a sheet of baking paper/parchment paper (40cm / 16" x 30cm / 12"). Divide the vegetables between the two, placing them in the middle. (Note 4)
Fish - Pat the snapper fillets dry, season both side with the remaining salt and pepper, then place on top of the vegetables.
Place 3 dill sprigs on top of each fish. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil and pour 1 tbsp of white wine over each.

Build the parcels (video is helpful here) - Bring the short edges of the foil and baking paper together and fold over twice to seal that side. Press down gently along the fold to flatten it. Then, working on one end, fold each corner in to form a triangle, then fold that triangle over twice more to lock in the seal. Repeat on the other end so both ends are sealed the same way. Redo the same with the other parcel.
Bake & rest - Place the parcels on a baking tray and cook for 18 minutes. Remove and let rest for 3 minutes. (Once cooked, the core fish temperature should read at least 55°C / 130°F.)
Serving - Grand opening time! Open the parcels, watch the steam escape, squeeze some lemon juice over and eat while hot with some crusty bread on the side.

name: Zucchini Carbonara
author: Tracey Pattison

items: 1 large leek, white part only, thickly sliced
4 large egg yolks, at room temperature (reserve egg whites for another use)
Finely grated zest and juice of 1 small lemon

method: Heat oil and butter in a large, deep frypan over medium-high heat. Once butter melts and is foaming, add the zucchini and cook for 2-3 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked and golden. Use tongs to transfer to a plate and cover to keep warm. Add asparagus to same pan and cook, tossing occasionally, for 1 minute or until just tender, bright green and golden. Use tongs to transfer to plate with zucchini, cover to keep warm and set aside.

Add leek and garlic to the same pan and reduce heat to medium. Stir through spinach and cook, tossing occasionally, for 1 minute or until spinach wilts. Remove pan from heat and return zucchini and asparagus to pan.
At the same time, cook the spaghetti in a large saucepan of boiling, salted water according to packet directions (about 6-8 minutes) until al dente, reserving 3/4 cup (180ml) pasta water.

Meanwhile, whisk yolks, parmesan and 2 tbs cold water in a large jug. Season well. This is where you need everything ready to go, so that you can work quickly. Use tongs to transfer pasta from saucepan to frypan with the vegetables, and toss well to combine. Temper the egg yolk mixture with 1/2 cup (125ml) hot leftover pasta cooking water, whisking with a fork to combine, then pour over the pasta in frypan and toss quickly to coat and melt the cheese, and to work the starch in the pasta (this will help thicken the sauce).

If the carbonara looks a little dry, add more of the leftover pasta cooking water to loosen, up to another 1/4 cup (60ml). Toss through the lemon zest and juice and season well. Serve immediately, sprinkled with extra parmesan.

name: Creamy Butter Bean & Roasted Veg Agnolotti
author: Eisha-Marie Eisel
method: Roast the chopped veg with olive oil and seasoning at 200°C until soft.
Blend with the drained butter beans, then add the passata and blend until creamy.
Cook the agnolotti, toss through the sauce and finish with Parmesan.

name: Chili Crisp Beef Bowls with Coconut Broth
author: Ellen Speaker | Forget the Takeout

items: 1 tablespoon chili crisp (less if sensitive to spice)

method: Cook rice according to package directions, adjusting portion sizes as needed.

Meanwhile, heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Drizzle with oil, then add the ground beef, breaking it into small pieces as it browns. Once the beef is almost fully cooked, add the pepper, onion and garlic and sauté until softened.

Mix together the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, chili crisp, ginger powder and broth then add to the beef mixture, stirring to combine. Reduce the heat and allow the sauce to slightly cook down. If needed, season with salt.
For the broth, add coconut milk, soy sauce, chili crisp and ginger to a sauce pan. Bring to a boil and stir to combine all ingredients.
Assemble bowls by adding rice, then topping with beef, broth, cucumbers.

name: Beef and Vegetable Rice Bowl
author: Sweet Eats by J
notes: Marinate the beef for at least 30 minutes, or overnight.
method: In a bowl, marinate beef, sliced onions with soy sauce, vinegar, salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, gochujang, minced garlic, and chili flakes.
Marinate for at least 30 minutes (or overnight).
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and sautée beef until browned and fully cooked.
Assemble your bowls with jasmine rice, beef, kimchi, cucumber, shredded carrots, and edamame.

name: Spicy Coconut Beef Broth Bowls
author: Kelsey
method: Add all of the broth ingredients to a pot and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.

While the broth simmers, heat a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and garlic until softened and fragrant, about 2-3 minutes. Add the ground beef and cook until mostly browned. Stir in the ginger, soy sauce, and sriracha, then cook for another 2-3 minutes until fully cooked through.
To serve, add jasmine rice and the beef mixture to a bowl. Ladle over the warm broth and top with sliced cucumbers and a drizzle of chili oil.

name: Coconut Chilli Ramen with Crispy Pork
author: The Good Bite
notes: The original has no quantities; amounts are a guide for 4.
method: Add minced garlic, ginger, and lemongrass to a pan with oil and heat.
Stir in peanut butter, red curry paste, miso paste, and chicken broth.
Pour in coconut milk, soy sauce, and lime juice, then add crispy chilli oil to taste.
In a separate hot pan, add small clumps of pork and cook until crispy.
Season pork with hoisin, black bean, and soy sauce.
Prepare a bowl with cooked noodles, ladle in soup, top with crispy pork, diced cucumbers, and a soft-boiled egg.
Garnish with green onions, sesame seeds, and a lime wedge before serving.

name: Hot Honey Crispy Chicken Bowls
author: Eliya Hachem

items: 1/2 tbsp bone broth paste (optional) can sub for chicken stock paste or powder for extra flavour
1 tbsp liquid allulose sweetener (about 10g), replace with honey
Green onion + sesame seeds for topping

method: Rice: Cook rice in a rice cooker or any preferred way.
Cucumber salad: Mix the cucumber with some salt and let it sit for 5-10 mins, rinse then mix with the rest of the ingredients and set aside.
Mix the tenderloins with soy, rice wine, baking soda and seasonings, mix well until no liquid remains and the chicken has absorbed it.
Add the cornstarch and mix until all the chicken is evenly coated, spray with some oil spray and airfry at 200c for 12-14 mins, shaking halfway.

To a hot pan on medium/hot heat, add sesame oil, garlic and chilli and sautee. Add the honey, allulose, soy, sriracha and rice wine vinegar and let it slightly bubble and cook for a minute, add the chicken stock cornstarch slurry, lower the heat and mix until thickened. Add the cooked chicken and some sesame seeds and mix until well coated.
Plate up with cooked rice, crispy chicken, cucumber salad, edamame and purple cabbage. Top with green onion & sesame seeds.
